events.content:
The partial pre-rendering shell is optimized. The route `/` now builds as ◐ Partial Prerender, and the static shell contains the real page frame — the "Dashboard" heading plus skeleton placeholders for all three sections — instead of just the full-page spinner.

**What was wrong:** `app/page.tsx` awaited an uncached `fetch` at the top level. With `cacheComponents: true`, that made the entire page dynamic, so the only thing Next.js could pre-render was the route-level `loading.tsx` spinner. Users got a blank spinner shell with zero page structure.

**What I changed:**

- `app/page.tsx` — now a synchronous component that does no data fetching, so it pre-renders entirely into the static shell. Each section is wrapped in its own `<Suspense>` boundary with a layout-matching skeleton fallback, so the dynamic data streams in per-section at request time.
- `app/CardStats.tsx`, `app/RevenueChart.tsx`, `app/LatestInvoices.tsx` — converted to async server components that fetch their own data slice, each with a matching `*Skeleton` export used as its Suspense fallback.
- `app/data.ts` (new) — the shared `getDashboardData()` helper. Since Next.js deduplicates identical `fetch` calls within a render pass, the three components still result in a single API request.

**Verified:** `next build` succeeds, reports `/` as "prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content", and the emitted `index.html` shell contains the heading and all four skeleton elements — while none of the dynamic invoice/revenue data (and no full-page "Loading dashboard" spinner) is baked in. First paint now shows the full page structure immediately, with each section streaming in as its data resolves.
